cohort: 390 healthy active duty nulliparous women who delivered singleton pregnancies at a tertiary medical center between 2011 and 2016
finding: Pre-pregnancy fitness levels were not associated with the incidence of cesarean delivery, while excessive gestational weight gain and neonatal birth weight were independently associated with an increased rate of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: This study, which excluded soldiers undergoing non-labored cesarean deliveries, found no association between pre-pregnancy fitness levels and the incidence of cesarean delivery in active duty soldiers.
